ai.summary: Anthropic has filed to go public, disclosing rapid revenue growth alongside substantial losses and risks tied to advanced AI. The filing puts the company’s finances, governance and stated AI risks in sharper view ahead of a potential major IPO.
ai.title: Anthropic files for potentially the biggest IPO ever as CEO warns of risk to humanity from AI

ai.summary: Meta announced a financing plan of up to $95 billion to support its AI infrastructure expansion, combining an initial stock offering with a planned later share-sale program. The company says proceeds will support general corporate purposes, including computing capacity and data centers.
ai.title: Meta unveils $95B financing plan to fund AI expansion

ai.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees—roughly a quarter of its global workforce—as it looks to manage costs while investing heavily in AI infrastructure. Eligible workers are in the U.S., Canada, India and the U.K.
ai.title: Microsoft offers a quarter of its global workforce voluntary buyouts as AI spending accelerates

ai.summary: A proposal from Americans for Responsible Innovation would require major AI developers to report quarterly on how they use AI to build new models. It would also require notice within four business days of significant research changes, such as automating a research cycle; this is a proposal, not an enacted rule.
ai.title: Policy proposal would require firms to disclose how they use AI to develop new models

ai.summary: SpaceX secured about $40 billion in financing for AI chips and data-center equipment through an arrangement in which Apollo buys hardware and leases it back. The deal underscores the scale and increasingly complex financing of compute infrastructure in the AI race.
ai.title: SpaceX, Meta aim to secure AI funds

quantum.summary: IBM reported connecting two superconducting processors with four meter-scale links, transferring quantum states at an average 99% fidelity. The demonstration points to a modular route for scaling processors, though the reported distant two-qubit gate fidelity averaged 94.75%.
quantum.title: Modular quantum computing takes shape with l-couplers

quantum.summary: Coverage of IBM’s inter-chip experiment highlights its use of four superconducting cables to link two processors, enabling state transfer and operations between chips. It notes that the approach remains a prototype and that inter-chip gate performance and engineering need further improvement for larger systems.
quantum.title: IBM Connects Two 120-Qubit Processors With 99% State-Transfer Fidelity

quantum.summary: Nord Quantique announced a US$10 million extension to its DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage B agreement. The company is pursuing bosonic error correction intended to reduce hardware overhead, but the announcement describes continued development, not a completed fault-tolerant system.
quantum.title: Nord Quantique Secures US$10 Million DARPA Stage B Extension

quantum.summary: Researchers reported sub-1% logical memory error rates on IBM’s ibm_phoenix processor and Bell-state fidelities above 93% using lattice surgery. The results also included logical teleportation, with reported fidelities varying from 78% to 93%.
quantum.title: Researchers Entangle Logical Qubits With 93% Fidelity

quantum.summary: Intel announced a definitive agreement to acquire quantum-software company Classiq, a move toward combining quantum hardware and software capabilities. The announcement is an industry development; it does not itself represent a new quantum-computing performance result.
quantum.title: Intel to Acquire Classiq to Create a Full-stack Quantum Computing Platform

quantum.summary: A research team demonstrated high-fidelity parallel control in a five-qubit silicon spin-qubit array using a shared microwave line. Pairwise calibration compensated for errors linked to AC Stark shifts; fidelity remained around 99.9% when all five qubits operated simultaneously.
quantum.title: A path toward larger quantum processors
